Read a spot-gauging archive

Source: R/read_gaugings.R
read_gaugings.Rd

Reads gaugings from a CSV file (or a data.frame) into a table with standard column names, whatever the original headers were called. It cleans nothing and removes nothing: every row of the file is returned, in order. What it does is read every column as text, turn placeholder text such as --- into a missing value, parse stage, discharge, date and time explicitly, and record in read_issue anything that did not parse, so a bad row is visible and not silently lost or changed.

The defaults match the column names of the Environment Agency WISKI-style gauging export (Station number, Date, Time, Stage, Flow). Use the mapping arguments for any other headers.

Dates are detected, not assumed. The format that parses the most values is used, day-first ahead of month-first when both fit (04/05/1970 is read as 4 May). The format chosen is reported in the message, with a warning when the choice was a default and could be wrong. Pass date_format (for example "%d/%m/%Y") to settle it.

Usage

read_gaugings(
  x,
  station_id = "Station number",
  station_name = "Station name",
  date = "Date",
  time = "Time",
  stage = "Stage",
  discharge = "Flow",
  date_format = NULL,
  tz = "UTC",
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A file path to a delimited text file, or a data.frame.

station_id, station_name

Character. Columns holding the station identifier and name. The name is optional: it is skipped if the file has no column called Station name, or if station_name = NULL.

date, time

Character. Columns holding the date and the time of day. time = NULL if there is none; a missing time is then midnight, with no note.

stage, discharge

Character. Columns holding stage (m) and discharge (cumecs).

date_format

A strptime() format for the date column, or NULL (default) to detect it.

tz

Time zone label for observation_time. Default "UTC". The clock time in the file is used as it stands, with no daylight-saving adjustment, so it is only as good as the file's own convention.

quiet

Logical. TRUE suppresses the summary message.

Value

A data.table, one row per row of the input, with these columns first: source_row (row of the data, header excluded), station_id, station_name, observation_time (POSIXct), stage_m, discharge_cms and read_issue (NA when the row parsed cleanly, otherwise the problems separated by semicolons). Every other column of the input follows unchanged, as text. The columns you mapped are not repeated; the file still has their original values.

Notes the function can add

station id missing, stage missing, discharge missing, stage not a number, discharge not a number, date missing, date not read, date outside 1800 to next year, time not read and time missing, midnight assumed. A stage of zero, a zero discharge or a discharge with no stage are not noted: they parse, and whether they are acceptable is a hydrometric judgement for a later check.

See also

read_operational_ratings() for the matching ratings export; compare_gaugings_to_rating() to check a rating against the result.

Examples

# A small archive as it might arrive: placeholder text, a blank
# station, an unreadable stage, and a stage of zero with a flow.
raw <- data.frame(
  `Station number` = c("10250", "10250", "", "F2405", "F2405"),
  Date  = c("03/02/1970", "05/05/1970", "29/05/1970", "06/01/1960", "12/01/1960"),
  Time  = c("12:47:00", "13:02:00", "", "00:00:00", "00:01:00"),
  Stage = c("1.6", "---", "0.85", "1.885", "0"),
  Flow  = c("53.3371", "9.738", "6.6824", "104.189", "0.425"),
  Remark = c("", "dry", "", "FALLING", ""),
  check.names = FALSE
)
gaugings <- read_gaugings(raw)
#> read_gaugings(): 5 rows, 2 stations, date format %d/%m/%Y.
#>   Rows with a note: 2. Most common: stage missing (1), station id missing (1), time missing, midnight assumed (1).
gaugings
#>    source_row station_id station_name    observation_time stage_m discharge_cms
#>         <int>     <char>       <char>              <POSc>   <num>         <num>
#> 1:          1      10250         <NA> 1970-02-03 12:47:00   1.600       53.3371
#> 2:          2      10250         <NA> 1970-05-05 13:02:00      NA        9.7380
#> 3:          3       <NA>         <NA> 1970-05-29 00:00:00   0.850        6.6824
#> 4:          4      F2405         <NA> 1960-01-06 00:00:00   1.885      104.1890
#> 5:          5      F2405         <NA> 1960-01-12 00:01:00   0.000        0.4250
#>                                            read_issue  Remark
#>                                                <char>  <char>
#> 1:                                               <NA>        
#> 2:                                      stage missing     dry
#> 3: station id missing; time missing, midnight assumed        
#> 4:                                               <NA> FALLING
#> 5:                                               <NA>        
gaugings[!is.na(gaugings$read_issue), c("source_row", "read_issue")]
#>    source_row                                         read_issue
#>         <int>                                             <char>
#> 1:          2                                      stage missing
#> 2:          3 station id missing; time missing, midnight assumed
